fields.title: «Polka»: the bill that outpaces revenue
fields.summary: Audience grew by 60%, revenue by 55%, infrastructure bill by 140%.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do you answer and what do you do? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. Over the year, the audience grew by 60%, revenue by 55%, and the infrastructure bill by 140%. The CFO is asking for an explanation and a plan.
fields.brief/objective: Explain the divergence between bill growth and revenue growth and return margins to the previous level.
fields.brief/constraints: Five weeks of work compete with the product roadmap.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you will answer the CFO and what you will do.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: If the bill grows faster than revenue, calculate per user
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Absolute infrastructure growth explains nothing: look at the cost per active user and break it down by drivers. Usually two or three cost items grow much faster than the rest, and their causes are mundane—forgotten retention, heavy images, new analytics. And the most valuable finding is often non-technical: a segment you serve at a loss.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Compute +45%, storage +180%, traffic +70%, analytics +260%, SMS +55%, acquiring +55%.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Added 22 new analytics events. Introduced high-resolution images. Event retention was not implemented—only order retention. Three chains connected with separate installations.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "Retention for events - a week, will free up about 40% of analytics storage. Image optimization - 3 days, will reduce traffic by about 30%. No audit of idle data has ever been conducted."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Cost per active user grew from 7.5 to 11.2 RUB. Gross margin dropped from 64% to 58%.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Idle resource review and quick optimizations
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Two weeks. Event retention, images, searching for forgotten resources, billing model.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: typically recovers 20–30%. Does not answer the structural question—why the bill is growing faster than revenue.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Build a driver-based cost model and tagging
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Build a driver-based cost model and tagging. Three weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: makes it possible to forecast and find causes moving forward. Saves nothing right now. The CFO needs an answer, not a process.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: The review recovers 20–30% of the bill as early as next month: event retention and prepared images hit the very items that grew disproportionately. The driver-based cost model shows where the next growth will come from—without it, the same thing will repeat in a year. Five weeks of work compete with the product roadmap, and this is the price that must be stated out loud along with the corporate tariff margin finding.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Revise the corporate tariff. Two weeks of negotiations.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: 270k in costs vs 340k in revenue—20% margin vs 58% on average. Three chains are subsidized by the rest of the product. Requires a price revision, which affects customer relationships.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not tie cost items to drivers
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not check cost behavior under growth
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not calculate margin by segments
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Bill growth is not broken down by drivers, so the root cause is not found
